ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a block diagram of a baseband binary PAM receiver. The input x(t) and noise n(t) are added at the adder to obtain r(t), then pass through the low-pass filter LPF to obtain y(t), and then pass through the sample-and-hold S/H to obtain y(t_k) at the sampling instant. After that, y(t_k) enters the threshold decision device and is compared with the threshold z: if y(t_k) ≥ z, it is decided as 1; if y(t_k) < z, it is decided as 0. Reasoning: The low-pass filter is ideal unit gain, the cutoff frequency is B = 1 MHz, and the two-sided power spectral density of the noise is S_N(f)=10^{-20} W/Hz. Therefore, the noise variance after the LPF is sigma_N^2 = 2B S_N(f) = 2 × 10^6 × 10^{-20} = 2 × 10^{-14}. The problem gives that the variance of the Laplace distribution of N_k is 2/alpha^2, so 2/alpha^2 = 2 × 10^{-14}, obtaining alpha = 10^7. Also z = a/2 = 10^{-6} V, so a = 2 × 10^{-6} V. If bit 0 is sent, then Y_k = N_k, and the error condition is N_k ≥ z = 10^{-6}; if bit 1 is sent, then Y_k = a + N_k, and the error condition is a + N_k < z, namely N_k < -a/2 = -10^{-6}. For the pdf f_N(n)=0.5 alpha e^{-alpha |n|}, the right-tail probability P(N_k ≥ x)=0.5 e^{-alpha x}, and the left-tail probability P(N_k < -x)=0.5 e^{-alpha x}. Substitute x=10^{-6} and alpha=10^7, alpha x=10. Therefore P(N_k ≥ 10^{-6})=0.5e^{-10}, P(N_k < -10^{-6})=0.5e^{-10}. The bits are equiprobable, so P_e = 0.5[0.5e^{-10}+0.5e^{-10}] = 0.5e^{-10}.

Consider a baseband binary PAM receiver shown in the figure. The additive channel noise \(n(t)\) has a power spectral density \(S_N(f) = \frac{N_0}{2} = 10^{-20}\ \text{W/Hz}\). The lowpass filter is ideal with unity gain and cut-off frequency 1 MHz. Let \(Y_k\) represent the random variable \(y(t_k)\).

\[
Y_k = \begin{cases}
N_k & \text{if transmitted bit } b_k = 0 \\
a + N_k & \text{if transmitted bit } b_k = 1
\end{cases}
\]

where \(N_k\) represents the noise sample value. The noise sample has a probability density function \(P_{N_k}(n) = 0.5\alpha e^{-\alpha|n|}\) (this has mean zero and variance \(\frac{2}{\alpha^2}\)). Assume transmitted bits are equiprobable and the threshold \(z\) is set to \(\frac{a}{2} = 10^{-6}\ \text{V}\). What is the probability of bit error?

method.method_draft: Describe the image first to confirm that the output sample y(t_k) is compared with threshold z. From the text, compute the post-LPF noise variance as 2*(1 MHz)*(10^-20) = 2e-14, so alpha = sqrt(2/(2e-14)) = 1e7. Since z = a/2 = 10^-6, a = 2e-6. Use the two conditional errors: if bit 0 was sent, error occurs when N_k >= z; if bit 1 was sent, error occurs when a + N_k < z, i.e. N_k < -a/2. Average these two equally likely cases: Pe = 0.5[P(N_k >= 10^-6)+P(N_k < -10^-6)] = 0.5[0.5e^-10+0.5e^-10] = 0.5e^-10.

method.method_draft: After describing the image blocks, note that the visual decision rule is a single threshold comparison on y(t_k). Because the text sets z exactly halfway between the two noiseless levels 0 and a, an error occurs only when the noise pushes the received sample across the midpoint. By symmetry, the unconditional error probability equals one half of the two-sided exceedance probability: Pe = 0.5 P(|N_k| > a/2). Determine alpha from the filtered noise power: variance = 2B S_N = 2e6*10^-20 = 2e-14, so alpha = 1e7. With a/2 = 10^-6, P(|N_k|>10^-6)=e^(-10), hence Pe = 0.5e^-10.

raw_record.original_question:
Consider a baseband binary PAM receiver shown in the figure. The additive channel noise \(n(t)\) has a power spectral density \(S_N(f) = \frac{N_0}{2} = 10^{-20}\ \text{W/Hz}\). The lowpass filter is ideal with unity gain and cut-off frequency 1 MHz. Let \(Y_k\) represent the random variable \(y(t_k)\).

\[
Y_k = \begin{cases}
N_k & \text{if transmitted bit } b_k = 0 \\
a + N_k & \text{if transmitted bit } b_k = 1
\end{cases}
\]

where \(N_k\) represents the noise sample value. The noise sample has a probability density function \(P_{N_k}(n) = 0.5\alpha e^{-\alpha|n|}\) (this has mean zero and variance \(\frac{2}{\alpha^2}\)). Assume transmitted bits are equiprobable and the threshold \(z\) is set to \(\frac{a}{2} = 10^{-6}\ \text{V}\). What is the probability of bit error?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a block diagram of a baseband binary PAM receiver. The input x(t) and noise n(t) are added at the adder to obtain r(t), then pass through the low-pass filter LPF to obtain y(t), and then pass through the sample-and-hold S/H to obtain y(t_k) at the sampling instant. After that, y(t_k) enters the threshold decision device and is compared with the threshold z: if y(t_k) ≥ z, it is decided as 1; if y(t_k) < z, it is decided as 0.

Reasoning: The low-pass filter is ideal unit gain, the cutoff frequency is B = 1 MHz, and the two-sided power spectral density of the noise is S_N(f)=10^{-20} W/Hz. Therefore, the noise variance after the LPF is sigma_N^2 = 2B S_N(f) = 2 × 10^6 × 10^{-20} = 2 × 10^{-14}. The problem gives that the variance of the Laplace distribution of N_k is 2/alpha^2, so 2/alpha^2 = 2 × 10^{-14}, obtaining alpha = 10^7. Also z = a/2 = 10^{-6} V, so a = 2 × 10^{-6} V. If bit 0 is sent, then Y_k = N_k, and the error condition is N_k ≥ z = 10^{-6}; if bit 1 is sent, then Y_k = a + N_k, and the error condition is a + N_k < z, namely N_k < -a/2 = -10^{-6}. For the pdf f_N(n)=0.5 alpha e^{-alpha |n|}, the right-tail probability P(N_k ≥ x)=0.5 e^{-alpha x}, and the left-tail probability P(N_k < -x)=0.5 e^{-alpha x}. Substitute x=10^{-6} and alpha=10^7, alpha x=10. Therefore P(N_k ≥ 10^{-6})=0.5e^{-10}, P(N_k < -10^{-6})=0.5e^{-10}. The bits are equiprobable, so P_e = 0.5[0.5e^{-10}+0.5e^{-10}] = 0.5e^{-10}.
